root_idea.summary: The root centers on ease, spaciousness, stillness, and an open or level spatial condition; it also has a distinct branch concerning terrain that may be depressed or elevated.
root_idea.development: The lexical evidence connects ease and stillness with gentle or continuous movement, while the spatial branch extends to openings, broad or level expanses, hollows, and elevations. Several derived forms develop these ideas into approach, reconciliation, enabling, and specialized nominal usages.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is presented under the normalized citation form رَهْوٌ.

senses.definition: An open, unobstructed passage or broad expanse; in the Quranic command, leave the sea open as a passage.
senses.usage_conditions: Quran 44:24 uses the noun in the expression رَهْوًا. The interpretation emphasizes making a broad way or open passage through the sea.
In Quran 44:24, this is an explicit alternative interpretation of leaving the sea still or calm.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To part or make an opening between the legs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal construction; this physical opening is also the basis for the Quranic expression involving an open passage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Easy, gentle, quiet, and continuous movement; of camels, movement in succession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to going or pace. The same lexical record also reports contrasting forceful movement, treated separately below.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Light, quick, or vehement movement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported movement sense that can contrast with the gentle or quiet sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stillness, calm, quiet, or motionlessness; also still or unmoving rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of such things as sea, heat, actions, and rain in broader Classical Arabic usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quietly and without constraint; willingly, voluntarily, or without being asked.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adverbial use describing an action or a gift performed without compulsion or solicitation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bird, to spread the wings without flapping them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I usage specifically applied to a bird’s manner of flight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach or draw near to something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may describe approaching puberty or virility.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid another in foolishness or stupidity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III usage equated with supporting or joining someone in folly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find or meet with a wide or ample place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV verbal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take as wife a woman described as wide in the vulva.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV marital and anatomical usage; the description belongs to this lexical construction, not to women generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To continue supplying food and drink to guests, out of liberality.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV causative construction concerning sustained hospitality.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To do well or perform properly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded as an admonition to a shooter or thrower who has performed badly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be gentle with oneself or show oneself mercy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV reflexive-directed construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become within someone’s power or reach, or become possible or practicable; to make something so.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The intransitive and causative constructions are both attested: a thing may become possible, or someone may make it possible for another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To leave something until it becomes still or motionless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IV construction of causing or allowing stillness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To persist or continue in eating the bird called رَهْوٌ, identified with a crane or similar aquatic bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized Form IV construction describing continual eating of that bird.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make peace or become reconciled with one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal Form VI usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become commingled, confounded, or confused.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form IX usage describing mutual mixing or confusion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A prepared food of grain or wheat with milk, made by rubbing or grinding the grain, pounding it, and cooking it with milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The preparation may begin with ground wheat or with ears of corn rubbed and bruised before milk is added.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An intervening space or gap between two things.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Illustrated by the space between the two humps of a camel of the falij type.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A terrain feature that may be a depression or an elevation, including a water-collecting hollow, a hillock, or, in one reported usage, a mountain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is explicitly reported with opposite topographical values; the depression may hold stagnant water, while the elevation may be a hillock or high ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A passage through a market with sellers seated along its sides.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical report attributed to a supplementary authority and not present in every copy of the cited lexicon.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wide, ample, or spacious; specifically, a well wide at the mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The well usage is a concrete application of the general spatial adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A derogatory epithet for a woman, especially one described as sexually indiscriminate or as having a wide vulva.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical and moralized usage recorded for the noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dispersed or scattered.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival or nominal description of something spread apart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A company or group following one another in succession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of people or horsemen, including a raiding party proceeding consecutively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bird, identified by some as a crane and by others as a similar aquatic bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is reported as رِهَاءٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A headcovering worn next to the head and liable to become dirty quickly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state or condition of elevation or depression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two opposite topographical values are both explicitly reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A depressed piece of land or ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal form for low-lying terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse with an easy back in movement; also a pacing horse in a reported colloquial usage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form and pronunciation are reported with variation in the lexical record.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wide or level tract of land, especially an even expanse or plain often associated with mirage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for broad, level terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dust-coloured or smoke-like hue or haze.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This sense is reported as an additional lexical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ample, unstraitened, pleasant, or easy circumstances; an easy journey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to life and to a journey characterized by ease.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Still or motionless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal or adjectival use separate from the description of an easy life or journey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Continuing or permanent, especially of food; the corresponding feminine form may be applied to wine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical comparison with رَاهِنٌ is recorded for the lasting-quality sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bee.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The designation is associated with the insect’s quiet manner of flying.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quick, swift, or fleet mare.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical record reports variant forms and plural formations for this specialized equine term.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The wide-mouthed well is covered as a concrete application of wide or spacious.
The quick or swift use is grouped with the independently attested rapid-movement branch.
The still or quiet adjective is grouped with the broader stillness branch.
Still rain is covered as a stated application of stillness.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the woman-specific entry.
The wide, even, and mirage-prone tract descriptions are grouped.
The preparation description is combined with the directly related food entry.

cautions: Quran 44:24 is retained with two lexically attested interpretations: leaving an open passage through the sea and leaving the sea still or calm.
The Quranic occurrence is the inflected form رَهْوًا; the public headword is normalized to the noun citation form رَهْوٌ.
